payload.rationale: Observed: GISS LOTI Jan–Aug 2026 anomalies average 1.224 C (sum 9.79). To exceed the contractual 1.28 threshold (displayed value ≥1.29, i.e., annual ≥~1.285), Sep–Dec must average roughly ≥1.41 C. The second condition (above 2025's 1.19) is effectively guaranteed if the first is met. Context: NOAA CPC (10 Sep 2026) reports El Niño strengthening with eastern Pacific SST anomalies exceeding +3.0 C and >90% chance of a very strong event in fall/winter 2026-27. Historically (2015, 2023), global monthly anomalies during the developing phase of strong El Niños rose ~0.15–0.25 C above the preceding summer in Sep–Dec; August 2026 is already 1.40. Applying that transfer assumption to Jun–Aug (mean ~1.28) or August alone suggests Sep–Dec averaging roughly 1.45–1.60, above the ~1.41 needed, but the margin is only a few hundredths on the annual mean, and single months vary by ±0.1. Too high if: August's 1.40 was a spike, the lag between ENSO and global temperature delays the bulk of warming into 2027, central-Pacific cooling noted in June–July damps the response, or monthly revisions shave values. Too low if: a record-strength eastern Pacific El Niño (+3 C) produces a 2023-style jump (Sep 2023 was ~+0.28 above Aug), which would make Sep–Dec averages of 1.5+ likely and clear the threshold comfortably. Net: moderately more likely than not, ~0.68.
limitations: Four months of 2026 data missing; estimate relies on analog transfer from 2015 and 2023 El Niño responses, not a fitted predictive model.
No explicit ENSO-to-GISTEMP lag model or forecast distribution supplied; monthly noise is ±0.1 C.
GISS monthly values are revised; threshold margin is only a few hundredths on the annual mean, so rounding and revisions matter.
Source excerpts were truncated; CPC statements interpreted from partial text.
